assumptions: Attempt costs are the frozen per-verifier means. Measurement variance is not propagated.
Every candidate is given the same synthetic expected capability, so expected coverage does not remove teams. This is not the production capability map.
The dependency registry is shared_unknown for the four names. Dependency groups do not enter the budget test.
Fixture decision losses belong to verifiers a, b, and c. They are overlaid onto every calibrated team of the same aggregation. They are not empirical roster payoffs.
Suppression rows stay in the fixture extract and are excluded from the overlay because the settings proposal sets suppression to unavailable.
resource_weight does not enter enumerate_strategies. The budget does.

budgets.derivation: Estimated cost of the cheapest two-verifier team under enumerate_strategies. At the easy/medium floor this admits only that pair. At the hard floor it admits nothing, because every size-3 team costs more.
budgets.name: restrictive

budgets.derivation: Estimated cost of the only three-verifier team that excludes confidence. Every confidence team costs more, so confidence is infeasible at both participant floors. Equality is feasible: enumerate_strategies rejects only a strict cost excess.
budgets.name: moderate

budgets.derivation: Estimated cost of the cheapest three-verifier team that includes confidence. This is the smallest cap at which the hard floor can field confidence. It is a boundary used to explain the confidence cost, not a fourth protocol level.
budgets.name: confidence boundary

budgets.derivation: Estimated cost of the four-verifier team. It equals the sum of the frozen means and is the smallest cap that admits every team. The sum is not a selected protocol budget.
budgets.name: permissive

coefficients.derivation: LossConfiguration.resource_weight allows zero. The penalty term is then identically zero. This is a decision-only reference, not a recommendation to drop cost from the protocol.
coefficients.name: no resource penalty

coefficients.derivation: Proposed uncertainty loss 0.2 divided by the frozen confidence mean. One confidence attempt then costs the same as one uncertain decision.
coefficients.name: low

coefficients.derivation: Proposed false-acceptance loss 1.0 divided by the frozen confidence mean. One confidence attempt then costs the same as one false acceptance.
coefficients.name: moderate

coefficients.derivation: Proposed uncertainty loss 0.2 divided by the frozen semantic mean. One semantic attempt then costs the same as one uncertain decision, so a confidence attempt costs many false-acceptance losses. Rule is not the denominator: its mean is under a tenth of a millisecond and would only inflate the same ratio.
coefficients.name: high

floors.implementation: Non-hard PlanningContext uses max(2, plan.minimum_count). The default easy and medium bands are (2, 2) and (2, 3).
The default hard band is (3, 4), and a hard plan uses plan.minimum_count. This context sets that minimum to 3.

label: SYNTHETIC / CONFIGURATION-SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS

loss_scale.role: Scale used only to translate milliseconds into loss. Not an approved coefficient.
